verdicts.quote: "Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs)."
verdicts.reason: Public OAuth2 is documented and intended for third‑party integrations; for a multi‑tenant agent acting on a customer’s account, OAuth2 is the appropriate primary method.

verdicts.quote: "Klaviyo free plan… Up to 250 active profiles and 500 emails per month" … "Start for free"
verdicts.reason: Free, self‑serve signup exists, and dev docs allow creating OAuth apps and sharing install URLs without a marketplace listing, so working credentials are obtainable self‑serve on a free plan.

verdicts.quote: "Campaigns 59 endpoints; Catalogs 55 endpoints; Profiles 38 endpoints; Segments 11 endpoints; Templates 17 endpoints; Webhooks 7 endpoints."
verdicts.reason: The reference shows dozens of resource categories with many endpoints across campaigns, flows, profiles, lists, metrics, catalogs, etc., indicating broad coverage.

verdicts.quote: "Klaviyo hosts the server at: https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp It signs you in with OAuth"
verdicts.reason: Klaviyo publishes and hosts an official MCP server (remote‑hosted), documented in the developer site and Help Center, for AI clients to operate on account data via OAuth.

verdicts.quote: "Note that only Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners can access and manage webhooks with our Webhooks API."
verdicts.reason: Buildable now with self‑serve OAuth and a broad API, but there are caveats: some features (e.g., Webhooks API) are plan/partner‑gated, and marketplace distribution requires app review even though private install URLs work without listing.
